text:
maria: Heads up — seeing repeated GPU attach failures in us-west1 over the last hour. Root cause looks like NVMe thermal oscillation causing IOPS collapse and then rapid recoveries, which is tripping our attach timeout path. Example from affected host (dmesg snippet):

maria: ```
[ 12345.678901] nvme0: thermal throttling assert
[ 12346.123456] nvme0: i/o completion delayed, qdepth 32 -> 2
[ 12346.223344] nbd0: write-timeout - requeueing
```

jordan: wow ok. is this across the whole AZ or just a rack? :thinking_face:

maria: mostly ap-southeast-west-1a nodes in the GPU pool. we see a periodic ~5min oscillation in iops. sample iostat window:```
Linux 5.10.0 (host-123)  
avg-cpu:  %usr %nice %sys %iowait %steal %idle
           12.3   0.0   7.1   75.2    0.0   5.4
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s  wrqm/s  %util
nvme0n1         1200.5  450.2  64000   18000     0.0    12.0  98.7
nvme0n1          20.1   10.3   1024     400     0.0     1.0   10.2
```

sam: that %util swing is brutal. any recent firmware or janitor changes?

maria: no firmware pushes in the last 48h. we did change the janitor scrub concurrency in us-west last night (reduced timeout -> higher parallelism). suspecting thermal feedback where parallel scrubs spike temp -> controller throttles -> iops collapse -> workloads backpressure -> GPU attach waits.

raj: good catch. can we correlate with our thermal telemetry? ops-sched, do we have recent fan curve changes?

ops-sched: fan curve unchanged. we did raise scrub concurrency for cost reasons (wanted faster clean windows). rolling back concurrency is low-risk — can do a canary in the eu-west cluster first.

jordan: should we divert new GPU provisioning away from the affected AZ until we have a fix? capacity is tight but safer. I can flip routing rules for 10m windows to drain attaches to other AZs.

maria: yes please. start diversion and mark the AZ in Console as degraded. I'll run a grep across nvme temps and scrub jobs to prove correlation.

sam: mitigation ideas: 1) throttle janitor concurrency 2) add temp-based backoff in janitor (avoid running heavy scrub if controller temp > 70C) 3) increase attach timeout and gradual retry 4) route attaches to healthy zones until backlog clears.

raj: agree. priority order: divert provisioning (low latency fix), rollback scrub change (medium), long-term: temp-aware janitor + smarter clean batching. Also we should notify SRE oncall.

infra-bot: [alert] GPU-POOL-ATTACH-Failures spike detected in us-west1-a — 78 failures in last 15m. Linked ticket: INF-4129

maria: creating INF-4130 to track rollback + telemetry dashboard update. attaching quick grep: ```
$ sudo journalctl -u janitor --since "1 hour ago" | grep -i "concurrency"
Jan 10 01:02:00 janitor[4456]: starting scrub batch size=12
Jan 10 01:02:01 janitor[4456]: starting scrub batch size=12
```

jordan: i'm kicking the diversion now and opening a short maintenance window on the console. will post status in 5m. :thumbsup:

tom: if diversion hurts latency for customers in us-west, we'd want to rollback after partial drain rather than leave it long. keep me posted on backlog numbers.

maria: agreed. I'll push a dashboard tile showing attach success rate and nvme temp overlay.

sam: TL:DR runbook: 1) divert attaches 2) rollback janitor concurrency in us-west 3) monitor temps & iops 4) implement temp-based backoff in janitor (RFC next week)

raj: fine. assign INF-4130 to maria + ops-sched, set priority P1 (because this is causing failed GPU provisioning).

ops-sched: rollback started — reducing scrub batch size to 3 on target AZ. patch applied to 12 hosts, rolling.

maria: thanks. early signs: iops variability down, attach failure rate dropping from 6% -> 0.5% on patched hosts. will report back after full rollback. :party_parrot:

infra-bot: [update] INF-4130 created, linked to INF-4129. Incident channel: #incidents-3231

jordan: diversion toggled off after drain, AZ marked degraded for 30m.

maria: last note — let's add a cheap probe: if nvme controller temp > 68C, pause new scrub batches for 10min. I'll draft PR for janitor tomorrow.

sam: good plan. also consider adjusting cost policy so we don't push aggressive scrubs in high-attach windows.

maria: yep. follow-ups: docs & postmortem after we stabilize.

jordan: thanks all. closing the loop in 30m unless we see regressions.
